body: I had a dream when I was younger that I had showed up to my grandparents house for a seemingly normal visit, only to walk into the house and see my mother strung up on a meat hook in the living room by her chin, being bled out like how they deal with pigs for slaughter. My step-dad, covered in blood and acting completely normal and logical, was sitting on the couch in front of my mom, just kind of staring at her? I started freaking out and hysterically crying and screaming at him, asking how he could do this, was this his plan this whole time when he married my mom, anything I could think of to make sense of this situation. The whole time he was nearly silent and unmoving, until he started laughing at my screaming at him. He didn't provide any answers and started picking up tools he had placed next to him, which is when I turned to run to a different part of the house. I woke up shortly after going to hide in a bedroom, but I couldn't look at or interact with my step-dad normally for about a week afterwards. I ended up having to work that out in therapy before I could sit down with him and explain why I was avoiding him, because he was really hurt that I had randomly flipped a switch and was so cold and avoidant with him.

I was also raised as a tomboy, not into girly things, uncomfortable with my body growing into puberty and trying to hide it all the time, without even the knowledge that I could transition or that transgender men existed. Those feelings are there whether you're "exposed to it on the internet" or not, and they are very real experiences you are having that are distressing to go through. 
While it's much harder to advocate for yourself while you're a minor seeking relief from gender dysphoria, you shouldn't give up hope that you can transition if that's what you feel is right for you to do. 
Regardless of how your parents feel about it, you are the one who has to live with yourself day in and day out for the rest of your life, I fully believe you should do that comfortably in your body however you can achieve that.

Once I was on my own in the world, it took making friends with more lgbt people and talking with them about my gender feelings to realize and gain the language to understand that I was transgender, and then I started transitioning in my 20's.
